statement: For every integer N>=4, residents dispersing on K_N and neutral mutants dispersing on K_N minus two vertex-disjoint edges under type-specific Moran birth-death have, at every singleton starting vertex, fixation probability <=1/N-4/[N^2(N-1)(N(N-2)+2)]<1/N. Uniform singleton averaging inherits the bound. Full arbitrary-G and matching-size>=3 questions remain unresolved.
contribution: Uniform all-N two-disjoint-deletion subclass theorem and a pointwise quantitative bound, extending the published one-deleted-edge Theorem A.1. Published N=6 numerical evidence is credited; the primary-source novelty search is bounded.
